descriptionText: Workflows that publish runtime artifacts (packages, releases, deployments) while using dependency caching are vulnerable to cache poisoning attacks. An attacker who gains write access to the cache (e.g., through a pull request in pull_request_target workflows) can inject malicious dependencies that will be used when building and publishing artifacts to production. This affects actions like actions/cache, actions/setup-go, actions/setup-node, actions/setup-python, and many others that cache dependencies. The vulnerability is particularly dangerous in workflows triggered by release events or that use publisher actions like pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish, docker/build-push-action, or softprops/action-gh-release. To mitigate, disable cache writes in publishing workflows by setting appropriate flags: lookup-only: true for actions/cache and Swatinem/rust-cache, cache: false for most setup-* actions, or removing caching entirely.
